findings.title: Cleanup registered for literal alias "alias", not the created IDPs
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` targets an IDP literally named "alias", not the one just created (`idp-alias-N`). The same bug is on line 425, where `idp-alias-20` is created. None of the 21 IDPs created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are removed after the test, and cleanup may also fail because "alias" does not exist. Leftover IDPs, including org-linked public ones, leak into later tests in the same realm. This can change login-IDP counts and make other tests order-dependent. The alias variable should be used instead.

findings.title: Login-cache invalidation on update uses the org-aware wrapped model as the original
findings.body: `update()` obtains the original via `getById()`, which returns the wrapper whose `isEnabled()` returns false when the linked organization is disabled. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` evaluates `getLoginPredicate()` on that wrapper. If the org is disabled, the original is treated as non-login. If the update also makes the IDP non-login (for example `hideOnLogin=true`), neither condition triggers and the login caches are not invalidated. The cached ID set still contains the IDP. When the org is re-enabled, the IDP appears on the login page even though it is hidden. The predicate should be evaluated on the raw stored model, not the org-aware wrapper.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate semantics changed without updating the search options or docs
findings.body: `getLoginPredicate()` now also requires that org-linked IDPs have BROKER_PUBLIC=true. `getLoginSearchOptions()` and the `LoginFilter` enum, which the Javadoc describes as the fields considered for login availability, do not reflect this. The REALM_ONLY and ORG_ONLY paths in `getForLogin` add BROKER_PUBLIC separately. The predicate and the search options are now two separately maintained definitions of "login IDP" that can drift apart. Any other caller of `getLoginPredicate()` silently gets stricter behaviour.
